VOPM said the problem is particularly acute in rural areas, where poverty, caste discrimination and limited access to legal assistance can leave minority families vulnerable.“This case has caused deep anxiety among Hindu communities in Sindh. Sindh hosts Pakistan’s largest Hindu population, particularly in rural districts where many Hindu families face poverty, caste discrimination and weak access to legal help,” it said.Rights groups have for years raised concerns over allegations involving the abduction, conversion and marriage of minority girls in Pakistan.VOPM cited data from the Centre for Social Justice, included in UK government material, which recorded 421 such cases involving minority girls and women between 2021 and 2024. Hindu women and girls accounted for 282 of those cases, while 72 per cent were reported from Sindh.The organisation said Pakistani authorities recorded at least 83 cases in 2024 alone, with Hindu girls making up 63 per cent of the victims.The concern extends beyond the figures. VOPM also referred to warnings by UN experts in 2026 that nearly 80 per cent of reported cases involving alleged forced conversion through marriage in Pakistan during 2025 took place in Sindh. About 75 per cent of the victims were reportedly Hindus.For VOPM, the immediate focus remains on the two sisters and whether they can speak freely about what happened to them.“Roopi and Seeta’s reported call to return home demands attention. Their protection, age, dignity, and freedom must come before every other consideration,” the VOPM noted.
Article Summary: Roopi, 13 and Seeta, 14, allegedly taken from Ibrahim Colony in Tando Allahyar district. They were allegedly converted to Islam and married to two Muslim men. Rights group calls for an independent probe and safeguards for the girls.

Article Title: Rear right wheel of Sita aircraft detaches during touchdown at Nepal's Juphal Airport- watch
Article Text:
Aircraft rear right wheel came off during landing

Poll Vote & Share your view Should flight operations at Juphal Airport be restored immediately even if repairs are ongoing? Yes, restore immediately No, prioritize safety 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

A Sita Airlines aircraft carrying 16 people suffered a runway mishap while landing at Juphal Airport in Dolpa district of Nepal’s Karnali Province on Thursday after its rear right wheel came off, officials said.According to PTI, the aircraft was carrying 13 passengers and three crew members, including seven foreign nationals, when the rear right wheel came off during landing. The aircraft had taken off from Nepalgunj for Dolpa and came to a halt on the runway at around 8:25 am local time.“The small aircraft carrying 13 passengers and three crew members met with an accident right on the runway after its rear right tyre came off,” Anil Raj Giri, deputy superintendent of police at the District Police Office in Dolpa, told PTI.The pilot immediately switched off the engine after the incident, preventing any further mishap. All 16 people on board were safe, while the aircraft suffered no major structural damage, PTI reported.However, the aircraft remained stranded on the runway, forcing authorities to suspend all flight operations at Juphal Airport. A Nepali Army aircraft approaching the airport was also forced to turn back.According to PTI, repair work on the runway is underway, with authorities arranging to fly technicians by helicopter to clear the aircraft and restore normal flight operations.
Article Summary: A Sita Airlines aircraft carrying 16 people suffered a runway mishap while landing at Juphal Airport in Nepal’s Karnali Province. The aircraft was carrying 13 passengers and three crew members, including seven foreign nationals, when the rear right wheel came off during landing. The pilot immediately switched off the engine after the incident, preventing any further mishap.

Article Title: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 men over 2019 Easter Sunday bombings
Article Text:
Seven years on, Sri Lankan court delivers verdict in Easter Sunday bombings case (Picture credit: AP)

15 convicted, nine acquitted

Death sentences and earlier convictions

Questions over intelligence failures

Separate investigation into former intelligence chief

A Sri Lankan court on Tuesday found 15 men guilty of involvement in the 2019 Easter Sunday bombings that killed more than 260 people and wounded about 500.The coordinated attacks targeted three churches and three hotels across the island nation during Easter services and celebrations.The Islamic State-inspired bombings were among the deadliest attacks in Sri Lanka's history. Forty-two foreigners were among those killed, according to the news agency Associated Press.The verdict comes more than seven years after the April 21, 2019 attacks, as separate investigations into the circumstances surrounding the bombings continue.The high court convicted 15 men who had been charged with plotting the attacks, while nine others were acquitted. The accused faced more than 23,000 charges, including murder, conspiracy to commit terrorism and offences involving firearms and explosives.Prosecutors said Naufer Moulavi, one of those convicted, masterminded the suicide bombings, the BBC reported.More than 2,300 people gave evidence for the prosecution, while investigators presented 2,076 pieces of evidence, including explosives, swords and firearms.None of the people believed to have directly carried out the bombings survived. The coordinated blasts at three churches and three hotels were attributed to two Sri Lanka-based Islamic militant groups.Authorities filed 23,270 charges against 24 suspects in 2021 over allegations that they planned or inspired the attacks.The charges were brought under the Prevention of Terrorism Act and included murder, conspiracy to commit terrorism, and firearms and explosives offences.Sri Lanka has not carried out an execution since 1976. As a result, death sentences are typically followed by life imprisonment.In July, a former police chief and a former senior defence ministry official were sentenced to death for failing to act promptly on foreign intelligence warnings about possible attacks.The two former senior officials were sentenced for criminal negligence linked to the bombings.The attacks prompted questions over security and intelligence failures. Sri Lankan authorities identified a major intelligence lapse, while parliament heard that a warning from India about possible attacks had not been properly shared with the authorities.In 2023, Sri Lanka's Supreme Court ordered former president Maithripala Sirisena to pay compensation to victims after finding him responsible for national security failures that contributed to the attacks.Sri Lanka's Catholic Church has also alleged, without providing evidence, that those identified as perpetrators were not the masterminds and that a wider conspiracy was behind the attacks, according to AP.A separate investigation involving former intelligence chief Suresh Sallay is also underway.Sallay is accused of orchestrating the bombings with Islamist extremists and denies the allegations.The claims echo allegations aired in a 2023 Channel 4 documentary, which included whistleblower testimony alleging that the attacks were allowed to happen to boost the popularity of the Rajapaksa family, which had long dominated Sri Lankan politics.Former president Gotabaya Rajapaksa, who was elected months after the attacks after campaigning on tackling Islamist extremism, has denied the allegations.He has been banned from leaving the country and has asked a court to prevent his potential arrest in connection with the ongoing investigation.For years, Sri Lankans have held demonstrations demanding justice for those killed and injured in the Easter Sunday attacks.
Article Summary: Sri Lankan court finds 15 men guilty of involvement in Easter Sunday bombings. More than 260 people were killed and 500 injured in the coordinated attacks. The Islamic State-inspired bombings were among the deadliest in Sri Lanka's history. A separate investigation into former intelligence chief Suresh Sallay is underway.

Article Title: Indian-origin climber Dhrubajyoti Guha, Nepalese guide killed in Manaslu avalanche
Article Text:
Dhrubajyoti Guha, based near Frankfurt in Germany, graduated in mechanical engineering from Bengal Engineering College, Shibpur (now IIEST Shibpur), in 2002.

TOI

An Indian-origin climber and his Nepalese Sherpa guide were killed in an overnight avalanche at Camp 3 on Mount Manaslu (8,163m) after they continued towards the summit while six other climbers turned back amid worsening weather, expedition organisers said on Sunday. Rescuers found Dhrubajyoti Guha and Fursemba Sherpa, both 47, buried inside their tent, taking the autumn season toll on the world’s eighth-highest peak to four.Guha, based near Frankfurt in Germany, graduated in mechanical engineering from Bengal Engineering College, Shibpur (now IIEST Shibpur), in 2002. He had worked with ABB, IBM, Pfizer and Nestlé and was an accomplished ultra-endurance trail runner with 32 UTMB World Series race finishes, including several over 100km. Sherpa was an NMA-registered guide from Nepal’s Makalu region who had summited Everest nine times and also climbed Kangchenjunga, Lhotse, Cho Oyu and Manaslu.Mohan Lamsal, managing director of expedition organiser Makalu Adventure, said conditions deteriorated as the group reached the higher camps. “Six other climbers who decided to retreat from Camp 2 are safe, but Guha and Sherpa decided to make an early summit attempt and headed for Camp III on Saturday evening,” Lamsal toldContact with the two was lost overnight. “We were alerted around 11.30am on Sunday after they stopped responding. We immediately sent four Sherpa climbers to Camp III to look for them. They dug through the snow and found both inside their tent, buried beneath nearly seven feet of snow,” Lamsal said.Continuing snowfall and avalanche risk prevented the rescuers from bringing the bodies to base camp. “I asked the rescue team to descend to the lower camps because it was not safe to remain there. We will try to bring the bodies down once the weather improves,” Lamsal said.Heavy snowfall began on Friday evening and continued through Sunday, with up to 60cm recorded at base camp, forcing hundreds of climbers to retreat or remain at lower camps. Some teams had begun ascending on Saturday in anticipation of a relatively favourable weather window from Monday, but meteorologists had warned of another spell of bad weather around Wednesday as a system developing over the Bay of Bengal was expected to affect the region.The deaths followed two earlier fatalities on Manaslu this autumn. Singaporean climber Lau Wee Seng, 50, died at around 6,000m while descending from Camp 2 on Sept 17, while Tashi Sherpa, 20, a Nepali high-altitude worker, was found dead inside a tent at base camp on Sept 5.Manaslu has drawn a record 480 foreign climbers this autumn, accompanied by more than 500 Nepali guides and support staff. The latest fatalities took the number of reported mountaineering deaths across the Himalayas and Karakoram this year to at least 24, making 2026 one of the deadliest for climbers in the region in recent years.
Article Summary: Dhrubajyoti Guha and Fursemba Sherpa, both 47, buried inside their tent. The autumn season toll on the world’s eighth-highest peak to four. Guha, based near Frankfurt in Germany, graduated in mechanical engineering from Bengal Engineering College, Shibpur.

Article Title: Sheikh Hasina holds talks with party leaders
Article Text:
Recent incidents have also indicated that the party is discussing its organisational future and Hasina’s possible return

DHAKA: The Bangladesh Awami League has put forth a nine-point set of demands and proposals, including reducing prices of essential commodities, ensuring uninterrupted supplies of electricity, fuel, gas and fertiliser, reopening closed industries and lifting the ban on activities of the party, reports Ahsan Tasnim.The demands were adopted at a virtual meeting of party's Central Working Committee held on Friday, with party president and former PM Sheikh Hasina delivering the keynote address.Recent incidents have also indicated that the party is discussing its organisational future and Hasina's possible return to Bangladesh in Dec this year. The govt headed by Tarique Rahman is under pressure on multiple domestic issues. The Jamaat-led opposition in Parliament is threatening to go the whole hog against the govt if its demands are not met.
Article Summary: The demands were adopted at a virtual meeting of party's Central Working Committee held on Friday. The govt headed by Tarique Rahman is under pressure on multiple domestic issues. The Jamaat-led opposition in Parliament is threatening to go the whole hog against the govt if its demands are not met.

Article Title: ‘Treated on floor, verandah’: Dhaka hospitals struggle to find space for dengue patients
Article Text:
Patients infected with dengue receive treatment at a hospital in Dhaka

Patients treated on floors, verandas

Dengue spreads beyond Dhaka

October could bring further rise

A sharp rise in dengue cases is putting hospitals in Dhaka under severe pressure. Over 747 new patients were admitted across Bangladesh in the 24 hours to 8am on Friday. The surge prompted some hospitals to treat patients on floors and verandas after beds filled up.According to a report by Dhaka Tribune, at Mugda General Hospital in Dhaka, 145 dengue patients were receiving treatment in a ward with a capacity of just 38 beds on Thursday. Doctors and nurses said the overcrowding was making it harder to monitor patients, administer medicines and provide emergency care.The directorate general of health services (DGHS) said no dengue deaths were reported during the latest 24-hour period. However, 79 dengue deaths have been recorded in the first 18 days of September alone.Since January 1, 59,147 people have been hospitalised with dengue across Bangladesh, with 176 deaths reported. A total of 54,838 patients have been discharged after treatment.At Mugda General Hospital, every designated bed in the dengue ward was occupied. Additional patients were being treated on the floor and veranda, while some beds were being shared by more than one patient.Afrin Akter, from Narayanganj, was among those being treated on the floor. She was vomiting intermittently and appeared too weak to speak properly as a nurse administered saline.Her mother said Afrin had suffered from fever and body aches for several days. After medicines failed to improve her condition, the family tried to get her admitted to several hospitals but could not find a vacant bed.They eventually reached Mugda General Hospital, where Afrin was admitted despite the lack of a bed.Nasima, sub-in-charge of the hospital, said patients were arriving every day from Dhaka and districts outside the capital.“Due to the bed shortage, patients are being admitted to the floor and veranda out of necessity,” she said.She said 145 patients were currently being treated in the ward against its capacity of 38 beds. Many patients, she added, arrive in critical condition, while early treatment can improve the chances of recovery.Dr Nurul Islam, deputy director of Mugda General Hospital, said the increase in dengue cases had pushed up patient pressure.“At present, services are being continued with the existing doctors and nurses, but additional beds and manpower are needed to handle the situation,” he said.“All the patients who are coming here are being admitted and provided treatment. Instructions have been given to every ward to provide proper treatment.”The latest DGHS figures show that the pressure is not limited to the capital.Of the 747 patients admitted nationwide in the latest 24-hour period, 216 were admitted outside Dhaka's city corporations but within Dhaka division. Another 61 were admitted in Dhaka North City and 40 in Dhaka South.Chittagong division recorded 180 admissions, while 92 patients were admitted in Mymensingh, 81 in Khulna, 52 in Rangpur and 25 in Barisal.August was the worst month for dengue this year, with 20,536 infections and 43 deaths reported.Entomologist professor Kabirul Bashar said forecast models indicate that the dengue situation could worsen further in October.Although Aedes mosquitoes become less visible as winter approaches, he said they should not be neglected.Referring to Bangladesh as a “country of mosquitoes,” Bashar said dengue cases were rising compared with previous years and warned that the situation could become more severe in the coming days.He called for greater public awareness about Aedes mosquito behaviour and stronger mosquito-control measures.DGHS director general professor Dr Prabhat Chandra Biswas said patients would be referred to private hospitals if government facilities exceeded their capacity.He said hospitals had been instructed to increase their bed capacity and that treatment facilities were also being strengthened at district and upazila levels in dengue-prone areas.Public health expert Dr Mushtak Hossain said treating patients alone would not be enough to control the outbreak.“The long-term effective solution is to destroy the breeding grounds of Aedes mosquitoes,” he said.He called for regular mosquito control, greater public awareness and early detection and treatment at the local level, along with adequate facilities in Dhaka and across districts and upazilas.
Article Summary: Over 747 new patients were admitted across Bangladesh in the 24 hours to 8am on Friday. At Mugda General Hospital in Dhaka, 145 dengue patients were receiving treatment in a ward with a capacity of 38 beds. Doctors and nurses said the overcrowding was making it harder to monitor patients, administer medicines and provide emergency care.

Article Title: From July Uprising leader to graft probe: Former Yunus govt advisor Asif Mahmud under scanner
Article Text:
Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain (Courtesy: Facebook)

Bangladesh’s anti-graft agency said Friday it has sought details of the financial transactions of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain, a prominent leader of the 2024 “July Uprising” that ousted the Sheikh Hasina government, as part of a money-laundering investigation.Mahmud and his wife have been accused of laundering $1.05 billion during his tenure as an adviser in the Muhammad Yunus-led interim administration, which governed Bangladesh following Sheikh Hasina’s ouster. The Yunus-led administration stepped down after the February 12 elections, which were won by the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP).“We have asked the Financial Intelligence Unit to provide comprehensive information on the financial transactions and assets of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain and his wife,” an Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) spokesman told reporters, PTI reported.A key allegation against Bhuyain is that he was involved in laundering Taka 11,000 crore across five countries, including Taka 4,500 crore allegedly siphoned off to Dubai. He is also accused of using illicit funds to purchase land in Portugal.Bhuyain has said that, if found guilty, he would rather serve a prison sentence than flee the country.The ACC has reportedly received more than 2,000 written complaints against advisors and officials of the interim administration.ACC Secretary Saidur Rahman Khan previously denied allegations that Bhuyain was being deliberately targeted, saying the proceedings against him were being conducted strictly in accordance with the law.The anti-graft body launched its investigation on September 2 and has since obtained documents from the local government and youth ministries, which Bhuyain headed during the interim administration.Before leaving office, advisors to the interim government disclosed their wealth statements. Bhuyain, who reportedly did not have a Taxpayer Identification Number before joining the administration, declared assets worth Taka 15.3 lakh at the time.
Article Summary: Bangladesh's anti-graft agency seeks details of financial transactions of Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain. He is a prominent leader of the 2024 “July Uprising” that ousted the Sheikh Hasina government. He and his wife have been accused of laundering $1.05 billion during his tenure as an adviser.
